newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cinemas shut to protest tax benefit removal.
newsitem.headline: Indian cinemas shut to protest tax benefit removal.

text.p: Cinema theatres in India's western state of Maharashtra closed indefinitely on Wednesday in protest against the withdrawal of a tax concession, film industry sources said.
They said the state's move to withdraw a tax benefit given to theatres would result in the doubling of ticket prices for filmgoers.
The state government decided to discontinue from January 1 the tax concession, made two years ago to theatres in commemoration of the centenary of world cinema.
Under the concession ticket prices ranged from 30 rupees (about US$1) to 100 rupees.
"It will affect everybody connected with the film industry -- producers, distributors, film industry workers and viewers," said Suresh Vora, a distributor.
Vora said small distributors would have to close at a time when only five percent of the total number of Indian films made were commercially successful.
Theatre owners said a number of people eking out a living near cinema houses, such as small caterers, would be badly affected.
There are about 1,300 cinemas in Maharashtra, of which nearly 100 are in Bombay, the state capital and centre of India's Hindi film industry.
